title: Ukraine's Starlink Is Back at Full Speed After a Week of Limits
summary:
Ukraine's satellite internet is working at full speed again, after more than a week of connection problems. The news came on Saturday, when tech billionaire Elon Musk said his company SpaceX had restricted the service, and Ukraine's leaders said speeds were back where they needed to be.

Starlink is a network of satellites that beams internet down from low orbit around Earth. In Ukraine, it helps military units stay in touch, especially in remote areas where regular phone and internet networks do not reach. Ukraine also uses a separate, more secure system called Starshield, which is controlled by the United States government.

Musk said SpaceX had restricted Starlink because, in his view, Ukraine had broken the service's rules by using it for military activity. He also said SpaceX had done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth. He denied being responsible for a problem with Starshield at the same time.

The connection trouble began last week, during a disagreement between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on oil sites inside Russia. United States President Donald Trump said he had told Musk to put the service back, after earlier denying that he had told him to limit it.

One Ukrainian official, Beskrestnov, pushed back. Writing on Telegram, he said Starlink terminals in Ukraine already had a speed limit of 70 to 90 kilometres per hour and did not work on Russian territory, so they physically could not be used for deep strikes.

Ukraine's defence minister, Yevhenii Khmara, said on Saturday that the military now had a stable connection, with drones able to reach speeds above 400 kilometres per hour. President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote that the speeds are now where they need to be. Musk did not explain in his post why SpaceX had made the change last week.
why_it_matters: It shows how important a good internet connection is for staying in touch, just like when your own Wi-Fi drops at home.

background_read: Satellite internet works by sending signals between small dishes on the ground and satellites flying in low orbit around Earth.
It can reach faraway places where phone lines and regular internet networks do not reach.
Armies also use it to stay in touch when they are far from towns and cities.
